statement: enforcer-cli's Command::Plan variant is a RESERVED clap subcommand (crates/enforcer-cli/src/main.rs dispatch()) that returns ExitCode::InternalError with an explicit 'plan subcommand is routed to arc-20; not wired in this skeleton' message -- there is no live enforcer plan new / enforcer plan check handler anywhere in enforcer-cli today, even though enforcer-plan's scaffolder (b01) and validator (b02) are both fully implemented and tested.
why: b05's acceptance block requires the /plan command emitter to 'dispatch to the real scaffolder + validator via the enforcer binary (not a stub)'. enforcer-cli is not in b05's owns: line (skills/plan/**, crates/enforcer-install/src/commands/plan.rs, crates/enforcer-plan/tests/self_validate.rs), so wiring Command::Plan's dispatch is out of scope for this pack -- but the emitter still had to target the real binary invocation syntax, not a workaround that calls enforcer-plan directly or fakes success.
howToApply: Build the emitted command body around the literal `enforcer plan new`/`enforcer plan check` invocation strings and assert on their presence (a `dispatches_via_real_binary` predicate) rather than trying to make the CLI dispatch actually work from an install-emitter pack. Document the CLI-side gap explicitly in the module doc so a future worker wiring enforcer-cli's Command::Plan handler knows exactly what syntax the shipped /plan command already promises callers.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-cli/src/main.rs dispatch() Command::Plan arm; crates/enforcer-cli/src/cli.rs Command enum doc comment

statement: b02's own validator.rs test module already establishes the exact pattern this pack needed for its own self-validate proof: a strict zero-findings assertion against the ONE workpack file the pack itself fully owns/controls, paired with a separate non-gating 'report read-only findings across all sibling workpacks' test that asserts total_ran > 0 (not hollow) but never fails cargo test on findings in files outside the pack's owns: line, persisting the report to proof/plan/<pack>-<name>.txt instead of printing (workspace lint bans print_*/eprintln! outside CLI crates).
why: This plan's own PLAN_STATE.md records 'No workpack is DONE' and a live scan of docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/workpacks/ turns up dozens of real PLAN-* findings across the 113 sibling workpack docs. A hard zero-findings assertion across every sibling doc would make b05 responsible for fixing ~96 findings in files it does not own; a hollow always-passing test would hide real drift silently.
howToApply: When a self-validate/self-host test's true scope is 'prove the live validator works, honestly, against real content this plan is actually authored in' rather than 'every sibling doc in the plan is compliant', split into (1) a hard-gated single-file test against the pack's own file, and (2) a non-gated persisted report against the full corpus that asserts the scan itself ran (total_ran > 0) but never asserts zero findings on files the pack does not own.

statement: skills/enforcer/SKILL.md already establishes the exact dual-audience convention the 2026-07-04 owner requirement asks for: a `<!-- ai-dense -->`...`<!-- /ai-dense -->` fenced YAML block immediately after the H1, followed by the full human-verbose prose body -- this predates the explicit owner requirement and did not need to be invented fresh for skills/plan/SKILL.md.
why: Following an already-established, already-shipped convention (rather than inventing a new dual-audience format) means the doc-parity check (skill_md_carries_both_dense_and_verbose_forms in tests/self_validate.rs) can assert on the identical delimiter pair a future cross-skill parity check would also look for, and any future typed-record migration of this authoring surface has exactly one delimiter convention to parse, not two competing ones.
howToApply: Before inventing a new markup convention for any new dual-audience doc, grep existing skills/**/SKILL.md for `ai-dense` (or similar) first -- reuse the exact delimiter strings and block placement (immediately after the H1, before the verbose body) rather than a per-skill variant.
